research_question: Can roadway, traffic, and crash data be combined to identify roadway segments associated with unusually high fatal and serious-injury crash patterns after accounting for traffic exposure and roadway environment?
unit_of_analysis: WSDOT traffic section-year, aggregated to roadway segments for final findings
exposure: AADT × section length × 365, used as an exposure proxy
statistical_model: Negative Binomial count model with traffic exposure offset and peer-environment context
unusualness: Upper-tail probability of observing at least the observed FSI count under the modeled expected count
persistence: Number of years from 2020–2025 with at least one FSI crash
finding_selection: Statistically unusual relative to modeled peer environment
At least 3 FSI crashes across the analysis period
At least 5 million units of cumulative exposure proxy
FSI observed in at least 3 years
interpretation_guardrail: SAFELENS identifies statistical associations and unusual patterns. It does not establish causation, determine fault, or prescribe an engineering treatment.
roadway_data_note: Roadway characteristics are reference/current roadway attributes applied to the historical analysis and should not be interpreted as exact historical roadway conditions for every crash year.
crash_context_note: Crash-context attributes describe reported characteristics of crashes associated with a finding; they are not causal explanations.
